_comment: Copy this to ~/.config/hanabi/config.json (or point HANABI_CONFIG at it) and fill in your values. With this file present you do NOT need any HANABI_* env vars. Env vars, if set, override the file. Delete the file (or set backend to "mock") to use the zero-config offline sample data.
_stream_note: OPTIONAL live token-by-token replies (Phase STREAM). Leave stream_path empty (or omit it) to disable http streaming — the app then uses the synchronous send path. When set (and backend is http), a reply is streamed over server-sent events: the adapter POSTs to stream_path and reads text/event-stream 'data: {json}' frames, mapping each frame's fields via the names below. All values are GENERIC placeholders; nothing about any real service is baked in. The offline mock streams with NO config at all.
_field_note: Field-name overrides map the adapter onto your backend's JSON shape. The defaults below match a sessions:[] + messages-with-blocks[] layout; change only if your backend differs.
_auth_note: OPTIONAL device-code login (Phase AUTH). Leave the two auth_*_path keys empty (or omit this whole block) to disable in-app login — then you supply the token above (or run the offline mock). When both paths are set AND backend is http AND no token is stored, hanabi runs an in-app RFC 8628-style device-code flow: it requests a code, shows you a short code + a URL to open, polls until you approve, then persists the bearer token to ~/.config/hanabi/token.json (mode 0600) so you stay signed in. All values below are GENERIC placeholders — fill in your backend's real paths/field names. Nothing about any real service is baked into hanabi.
